summary.short: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025 (selected AI-related sections). Directs the Department of Defense and the NSA to set up AI initiatives, centers and pilots, requires related reports, and conditionally bars DoD procurement of certain foreign-made unmanned ground vehicles. Deadlines generally run from enactment.
summary.long: Extract of selected sections of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025 on artificial intelligence (AI) and related defense technology. Section 6504 requires the National Security Agency to establish an AI Security Center within 90 days of enactment, with disestablishment possible after three years. Sections 1531-1534 and 1087 direct the Department of Defense (DoD) to set up an AI human factors initiative, expand high-performance computing infrastructure with a roadmap, plan AI training-data budgeting, evaluate an AI-enabled weapon systems center of excellence, and establish a multilateral AI working group ending 30 September 2028. Sections 221, 222 and 232-237 and 1007 set AI workforce, education, maintenance-data, target-recognition, biotechnology and audit pilot requirements, mostly as plans, briefings and reports. Section 1078(b) bars DoD from procuring or operating unmanned ground vehicles made by covered foreign entities one year after a required report, unless a national-interest exception applies. Sections 1066, 1514 and 1515 require reports on lethal autonomous weapons, multi-cloud cybersecurity and mobile-device protections. Section 1031 requires Navy maritime autonomy standards within 180 days. Section 6506 adds AI to intelligence-community talent-exchange focus areas. The extract sets no fines or penalties.

Typos in the text: Sec. 236(d)(2) reads 'the date of the on which'; Sec. 221(c)(4) reads 'the ate of the briefing'.
